name: fastk
description: K-mer counter for high-fidelity shotgun datasets

repo.name: FASTK
repo.description: A fast K-mer counter for high-fidelity shotgun datasets

readme.summary: Thorough technical reference for a specialized bioinformatics tool, but lacks installation instructions, practical examples, and any troubleshooting guidance.
readme.top_issue: No installation instructions whatsoever — a new user has no idea how to build or install the tool.

injection_risks.description: The function hopen() is used to open a file, but it does not seem to be vulnerable to injection attacks as the filename comes from a trusted source (hts_idx_getfn()). However, if an attacker can manipulate the input to hts_idx_getfn(), they may be able to inject malicious filenames.

The function zlib_mem_inflate() is used to decompress data, but it does not seem to be vulnerable to injection attacks as the input comes from a trusted source (the index file). However, if an attacker can manipulate the input to zlib_mem_inflate(), they may be able to inject malicious data.

critical_findings: Potential injection risk in the hopen() function
Lack of input validation in the cram_index_load() function
security.summary: The code has some potential security issues, including a low-risk injection vulnerability and lack of input validation, but overall it appears to be relatively secure.

common_complaints: Segmentation faults and crashes (small data, HiFi readsets, gzipped input mishandling)
Compilation issues with modern compilers (clang 18, _GNU_SOURCE missing)
File format conversion limitations (binary .hist files, no Jellyfish/KMC conversion)
Operational issues with merged libraries and k-mer accuracy
Lack of package manager distribution (conda, official docker)
sentiment.summary: FastK is a valued but neglected project with critical unresolved bugs (crashes from 2022) and feature requests (conda, releases) open for 3+ years, indicating slow/sporadic maintenance despite user appreciation for its speed.

red_flags: Occasional dismissive tone towards new contributors
communication.summary: The maintainer is generally helpful and clear, but occasionally shows a dismissive attitude towards new contributors.

concerns: 18 open issues with no closed issues in 6 months indicates issues are not being addressed
No pull requests merged in 6 months despite a recent commit
No active contributors in the past 6 months
Unknown last release - no visible release cadence
positive_signals: Recent commit activity 2 months ago shows the repository is not completely abandoned
maintenance.summary: The package exhibits minimal maintenance with a recent commit but stalled issue resolution and zero contributor activity over 6 months, indicating the project is in decline or deprioritized.
